'''Symington:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} '''Basha:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Fife Symington]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Fife Symington]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsAZ}} The '''1994 Arizona gubernatorial election''' took place on November 8, 1994, for the post of [[List of governors of Arizona|Governor of Arizona]]. [[Fife Symington]], the incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Governor of Arizona]], defeated the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Eddie Basha]] to win a second term in office. However, Symington resigned in 1997 due to a federal indictment on corruption charges. ==Republican primary== In the Republican primary, incumbent Governor Fife Symington was challenged by businesswoman [[Barbara Barrett]], wife of business executive [[Craig Barrett (chief executive)|Craig Barrett]]. Symington announced his primary campaign by stating, "I vowed to get state spending under control, reduce taxes and do my best to promote economic development and restore strength to the economy. I think I am in a strong position because I accomplished my goals."{{cite web |url=http://tucsoncitizen.com/morgue2/1994/09/09/181218-governor-race-nears-first-stage/ |title=Governor race nears first stage |author=Pittman, David |access-date=May 10, 2017 |date=September 9, 1994 |publisher=Tucson Citizen}} Barrett spent more than $1 million of her own money in the attempt to defeat Symington, who she stated she did not dislike personally, but simply felt that she could do a better job as governor. On September 13, 1994, Symington defeated Barrett in the primary by a margin of 68% to 32%.{{cite web |url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=36911 |title=AZ Governor – R Primary Race – Sep 13, 1994 |publisher=Our Campaigns |access-date=May 10, 2017}} Political analysts stated that Barrett had failed to distinguish herself from the incumbent governor, and ran a flawed campaign. ===Candidates=== * [[Barbara Barrett]], businesswoman * [[Fife Symington]], incumbent governor ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title=Republican primary results {{cite web|url=https://azmemory.azlibrary.gov/nodes/view/102692|title=State of Arizona Official Canvass Primary Election - September 13, 1994|publisher=Arizona Secretary of State|access-date=2024-07-14}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = [[Fife Symington]] (incumbent) |votes = 202,588 |percentage = 68.14% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = [[Barbara Barrett]] |votes = 94,740 |percentage = 31.86% }} {{Election box total no change |votes = 297,328 |percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==Democratic primary== In the Democratic primary, 1990 Democratic gubernatorial nominee and former Phoenix Mayor [[Terry Goddard]] attempted to seek the Democratic nomination once again, but was challenged by [[Paul Johnson (American politician)|Paul Johnson]], who was also a former mayor of Phoenix, and [[Arizona Board of Regents]] member [[Eddie Basha]], more famous for his involvement with the grocery store chain [[Bashas']]. In the primary held on September 13, Basha defeated Goddard by a very small margin, with Johnson receiving a sizable level of support as well. ===Candidates=== * [[Eddie Basha]], Arizona Board of Regents and businessman * [[Terry Goddard]], former mayor of Phoenix and 1990 Democratic gubernatorial nominee * [[Paul Johnson (American politician)|Paul Johnson]], former mayor of Phoenix ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title=Democratic primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Eddie Basha]] |votes = 96,613 |percentage = 36.82% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Terry Goddard]] |votes = 92,239 |percentage = 35.16% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Paul Johnson (American politician)|Paul Johnson]] |votes = 73,512 |percentage = 28.02% }} {{Election box total no change |votes = 262,364 |percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== Following the 1990 election, in which a [[two-round system|run-off election]] was held in order to deter the possibility of a candidate winning with less than a plurality of all of the votes cast, as was the case with the [[1986 Arizona gubernatorial election|1986 election]] in which [[Evan Mecham]] was elected with only 39.96% of the vote, the 1994 election did not have a runoff. This was due to a measure that was approved by voters to eliminate the runoff system, which was marred by a longer than usual campaign and issues surrounding the date of when the runoff should be held.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bT2cpuf8OaMC&q=arizona+repeals+runoff+amendment+symington+1992&pg=PA78 |title=Arizona Politics & Government: The Quest for Autonomy, Democracy, and Development |author=Berman, David |access-date=May 10, 2017 |date=1998|isbn=0803212887 }} ===Results=== {{Election box begin | title=Arizona gubernatorial election, 1994{{cite web|url=https://azmemory.azlibrary.gov/nodes/view/102691|title=State of Arizona Official Canvass General Election - November 8, 1994|publisher=Arizona Secretary of State|access-date=2024-07-14}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link| |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = [[Fife Symington]] (incumbent) |votes = 593,492 |percentage = 52.54% |change = +0.18% }} {{Election box candidate with party link| |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Eddie Basha]] |votes = 500,702 |percentage = 44.33% |change = -3.31% }} {{Election box candidate with party link| |party = Arizona Libertarian Party |candidate = [[John A.
